1	---
2	title: Re-running workflows and jobs
3	shortTitle: Re-run workflows and jobs
4	intro: You can re-run a workflow run, all failed jobs in a workflow run, or specific jobs in a workflow run up to 30 days after its initial run.
5	permissions: People with write permissions to a repository can re-run workflows in the repository.
6	redirect_from:
7	  - /actions/managing-workflow-runs/re-running-a-workflow
8	  - /actions/managing-workflow-runs/re-running-workflows-and-jobs
9	  - /actions/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-workflow-runs/re-running-workflows-and-jobs
10	  - /actions/how-tos/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-workflow-runs/re-running-workflows-and-jobs
11	versions:
12	  fpt: '*'
13	  ghes: '*'
14	  ghec: '*'
15	category:
16	  - Manage and monitor workflow runs
17	contentType: how-tos
18	---
19	
20	Re-runs use the privileges of the actor who initially triggered the workflow, not the privileges of the actor who initiated the re-run. The workflow will also use the same `GITHUB_SHA` (commit SHA) and `GITHUB_REF` (git ref) of the original event that triggered the workflow run.
21	
22	A workflow run can be re-run a maximum of 50 times. This limit includes both full re-runs and re-runs of a subset of jobs.
23	
24	## Re-running all the jobs in a workflow
25	
26	{% webui %}
27	
28	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-repo %}
29	{% data reusables.repositories.actions-tab %}
30	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-workflow %}
31	{% data reusables.repositories.view-run %}
32	1. In the upper-right corner of the workflow, re-run jobs.
33	
34	   * If any jobs failed, select the **{% octicon "sync" aria-hidden="true" aria-label="sync" %} Re-run jobs** dropdown menu and click **Re-run all jobs**.
35	   * If no jobs failed, click **Re-run all jobs**.
36	
37	{% data reusables.actions.enable-debug-logging %}
38	
39	{% endwebui %}
40	
41	{% cli %}
42	
43	1. To re-run a failed workflow run, use the `run rerun` subcommand, replacing `RUN_ID` with the ID of the failed run that you want to re-run. If you don't specify a `run-id`, {% data variables.product.prodname_cli %} returns an interactive menu for you to choose a recent failed run.
44	
45	    ```shell copy
46	    gh run rerun RUN_ID
47	    ```
48	
49	    {% data reusables.actions.enable-debug-logging-cli %}
50	
51	    ```shell copy
52	    gh run rerun RUN_ID --debug
53	    ```
54	
55	1. To view the progress of the workflow run, use the `run watch` subcommand and select the run from the interactive list.
56	
57	    ```shell copy
58	    gh run watch
59	    ```
60	
61	{% endcli %}
62	
63	## Re-running failed jobs in a workflow
64	
65	{% webui %}
66	
67	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-repo %}
68	{% data reusables.repositories.actions-tab %}
69	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-workflow %}
70	{% data reusables.repositories.view-run %}
71	1. In the upper-right corner of the workflow, select the **{% octicon "sync" aria-hidden="true" aria-label="sync" %} Re-run jobs** dropdown menu, and click **Re-run failed jobs**.
72	{% data reusables.actions.enable-debug-logging %}
73	
74	{% endwebui %}
75	
76	{% cli %}
77	
78	To re-run failed jobs in a workflow run, use the `run rerun` subcommand with the `--failed` flag. Replace `RUN_ID` with the ID of the run for which you want to re-run failed jobs. If you don't specify a `run-id`, {% data variables.product.prodname_cli %} returns an interactive menu for you to choose a recent failed run.
79	
80	```shell
81	gh run rerun RUN_ID --failed
82	```
83	
84	{% data reusables.actions.enable-debug-logging-cli %}
85	
86	```shell
87	gh run rerun RUN_ID --failed --debug
88	```
89	
90	{% endcli %}
91	
92	## Re-running a specific job in a workflow
93	
94	{% webui %}
95	
96	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-repo %}
97	{% data reusables.repositories.actions-tab %}
98	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-workflow %}
99	{% data reusables.repositories.view-run %}
100	1. Under the "Jobs" section of the left sidebar, next to the job that you want to re-run, click {% octicon "sync" aria-label="The re-run icon" %}.
101	
102	{% data reusables.actions.enable-debug-logging %}
103	
104	{% endwebui %}
105	
106	{% cli %}
107	
108	To re-run a specific job in a workflow run, use the `run rerun` subcommand with the `--job` flag. Replace `JOB_ID` with the ID of the job that you want to re-run.
109	
110	```shell
111	gh run rerun --job JOB_ID
112	```
113	
114	{% data reusables.actions.enable-debug-logging-cli %}
115	
116	```shell
117	gh run rerun --job JOB_ID --debug
118	```
119	
120	{% endcli %}
121	
122	## Reviewing previous workflow runs
123	
124	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-repo %}
125	{% data reusables.repositories.actions-tab %}
126	{% data reusables.repositories.navigate-to-workflow %}
127	{% data reusables.repositories.view-run %}
128	1. To the right of the run name, select the **Latest** dropdown menu and click a previous run attempt.

content.text:
No — this documentation doesn't offer a per-step or per-job flag to force re-execution during "Re-run failed jobs." That feature runs only the jobs that failed (or their dependents), skipping successful jobs entirely.

Source: `content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md`, section "Re-running failed jobs in a workflow." Your workaround would be to use **Re-run all jobs** instead (same section, "Re-running all the jobs in a workflow") so the setup step always executes.
